THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County moved toward a legal fight with Alliant Energy over the Hub City Wind Project, while Weston's board passed a contested 2027 budget on a 4-3 vote and Wausau's Plan Commission deadlocked on a downtown rezoning.

  • Marathon County Board voted unanimously to seek outside legal counsel and refer strategy on the Alliant Energy wind project Joint Development Agreement to the executive committee, which will also solicit input from Farmland First and Wisconsinites for Local Control.
  • The Village of Weston adopted its 2027 operating budget and capital funds budgets on 4-3 votes, with three trustees dissenting over borrowing levels and the use of TIF closure funds.
  • Wausau's Plan Commission split 2-2 on rezoning 317 East Kent Street from urban mixed-use to heavy industrial, sending the unresolved question to the full City Council for a decision at its December 8 meeting.
  • Wausau's Board of Public Works received 15 demolition bids for the former MBX South building at 207 North 1st Avenue but made no award, pending confirmation of funding.
  • The Wausau Transit Commission unanimously approved participation in a transit development planning study backed by a $120,000 state grant, and greenlit an RFP for new fare boxes and bids for facility door and ceiling replacements.
  • The Wausau School Board is set to vote Monday on 2027-2028 4K program agreements and secondary social studies curriculum updates, and to meet in closed session to consider preliminary contract non-renewals.

Coming up: Tuesday brings a full slate in Wausau, including a Common Council meeting at 6:30 p.m. — where the city's Finance Committee convenes beforehand at 5:15 p.m. — and a Marathon County Board meeting Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. that could see further action on the Alliant Energy wind project dispute.
